problem: ISS-3012 Phase 2 (structural half; operator completed the live-data cleanup 2026-07-26). Two defects let the 2026-07-18 shadow-field cruft (queue_length / queue_depth / next_queue_id:587) sit unnoticed on priority-queue.json for 6 days: (1) lint-decider-surfaces.js lines 209/219 read next_queue_id as a FALLBACK for next_id. The stale-low shadow value (587 vs canonical 591) was a poisoned fallback in the trust path: masked while next_id is present, but any future edit that dropped or nulled next_id would silently authorize reuse of queue_ids 587-590 — the exact qid-collision class PROP-089 exists to prevent. (2) Nothing lints the queue file's own top-level field-set for schema conformance — the lint validates items[] and next-id monotonicity but accepts arbitrary unknown/stale shadow fields, so operator/decider edits can silently reintroduce cruft. Evidence: ISS-3012 (found_by curmudgeon-verify + operator-cowork 2026-07-24); live-file state before cleanup per issue description; current live top-level keys enumerated by tinker 2026-07-28 from clone HEAD 638f04e.

proposed_fix.summary: Three-part hardening, all operator-applied in one commit. (a) next_id becomes REQUIRED on priority-queue.json: the next_queue_id fallback is deleted on both the local and base read paths, and a missing next_id is a blocking violation (kind 'next_id-missing'). Fail-closed replaces poisoned-fallback. (b) A top-level schema-conformance check rejects any field not in a canonical allowlist (kind 'unknown-top-level-field'), derived from DATA-SCHEMAS.md + the operator-ratified live field-set (includes description, schedule_state, depth, last_updated_by which were undocumented). Gated by a PROP-106-convention shadow flag (presence = log-only soak, absence = enforce) shipped PRESENT for a 7-day soak. (c) DATA-SCHEMAS.md's 'Live file top-level fields' list is updated to match the allowlist exactly, with a same-change discipline note, and the new flag is classified in build.js OWNERSHIP + workspace-sync.md NEVER_PUSH + CLAUDE.md per the file-ownership rule.

application_notes: Apply from a clean clone (lint-decider-surfaces.js is git-owned source code, NEVER_PUSH). After applying, sanity-run: (1) `node monitor/scripts/lint-decider-surfaces.js` from the clone root against current HEAD — expect pass with zero SHADOW lines (live file's 17 top-level keys are all in the allowlist); (2) `node monitor/scripts/lint-decider-surfaces.js --replay 3d9675d` — expect the historical drift catches unchanged; (3) temporarily add a bogus top-level key to a scratch copy and confirm the SHADOW line prints with the flag present and blocks with it absent. Then `node build.js publish` so the flag + script reach FUSE.
tradeoffs: GAIN: the poisoned-fallback path is gone (fail-closed on missing next_id), and shadow-field reintroduction is detected at push time instead of by a curmudgeon-verify no-op observation 6 days later. Docs and lint are forced into lockstep by the same-change rule. COST/RISK: (1) an allowlist is a maintenance surface — any legitimately new top-level field now requires touching DATA-SCHEMAS.md + the lint together; forgetting blocks decider's push (mitigated by the 7-day shadow soak and by the violation message saying exactly what to do). (2) next_id-missing is deliberately not flag-gated; if some unknown legacy flow pushes a queue file without next_id it will be blocked — judged correct because that flow would have been silently corrupting allocation via the 587 fallback anyway. (3) The operator-retained `depth` field is ratified into the schema rather than removed; if it drifts from queue.length the lint will NOT catch it (display-only field, documented as such). Alternative considered and rejected: flooring the next_queue_id fallback at max(live∪archive qid) — keeps a second source of truth alive for no benefit; no current writer maintains next_queue_id, so requiring next_id is strictly simpler.
estimated_impact: Risk reduction on the queue_id-allocation trust path (the PROP-089 collision class). Zero steady-state token cost: the check is ~15 lines of node in an already-running pre-push script. Closes ISS-3012's remaining scope; the decider can close the ISS when this PROP is applied.
why_human_needed: Two ratification calls: (a) confirm the 17-field allowlist — especially that `depth` and `last_updated_by` stay canonical (operator kept them in the 2026-07-26 cleanup; removing them instead would shrink the allowlist and this PROP's DATA-SCHEMAS text) — and (b) remove the shadow flag after the 7-day soak. Also touches CLAUDE.md + build.js + workspace-sync.md, which are operator-applied surfaces (tinker does not self-apply changes to the decider pre-push trust path).
